title: Ramadan, the fasting month
hookLine: a month of fasting from dawn to sunset, with prayer and generosity (Quran 2:183)

cards: A few minutes before sunset in a city apartment. The table is set, but no one's eating: a plate of dates, a jug of water, soup on the stove.

The whole family watches the clock, or listens for the call to prayer from the mosque down the street. Nobody has eaten or drunk anything since before dawn, not even a sip of water, and it's been a long, hot day.
Then the call comes, someone passes the dates, and a whole city breaks its fast in the same minute.

teach.h: A MONTH THAT MOVES WITH THE MOON.
teach.b: Ramadan is a month of the Islamic calendar, which follows the moon, so it comes a little earlier each year and moves through every season. Fasting in it is the fourth pillar of Islam.

The Qur'an gives the command, in Marmaduke Pickthall's 1930 translation: "O ye who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil)."
Even as for those before you: the fast stands alongside the fasting of earlier believers. From dawn to sunset, adult Muslims who are able go without food, drink and marital relations.
There are exemptions: the sick, travelers, the elderly, those pregnant or nursing, children.
A pre-dawn meal, suhur, starts the day; iftar ends it, often with dates and water, as tradition says the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, did. Why this month?

teach.h: THE MONTH THE QUR'AN CAME DOWN.
teach.b: The Qur'an says it's the month the Qur'an was sent down, and some aim to recite all of it during the month, with extra night prayers in the mosque.
Tradition places in its last ten nights the Night of Power, which the Qur'an calls better than a thousand months.
And yesterday's thread returns: a hadith in Bukhari says that if someone fasts but doesn't give up false speech and acting on it, God has no need of their giving up food and drink.
The hunger is meant to teach: patience, gratitude, what hunger is like for the poor. The month ends with Eid al-Fitr, a feast. The week, line by line.
Shahada: one. Salat: five pauses. Dhikr: hearts find rest.
Rahman: begin with mercy. Zakat: purified by giving. Good character: best in character.

how: During Ramadan adult Muslims who are able fast from dawn to sunset, eat suhur before dawn and break the fast at iftar, often with dates and water, add night prayers, give generously, and celebrate Eid al-Fitr at the end.

games.why: Sahih al-Bukhari 1903: the fast is meant to change speech and conduct, not only appetite.

practice: Notice your body right now: any hunger, any thirst, any restlessness. Don't fix it; just watch it.
Then think of someone for whom this feeling isn't chosen and doesn't end at sunset, let the hunger teach you something about them, and if you pray, pray for them.
